verify_r54_review.py.description: Standard-library deterministic audit of the frozen R54 publication artifact and result records

blocking_findings: The directed theorem and verification architecture are representation neutral; R54 does not identify a neural computational advantage.
The final actual-policy comparisons are unresolved and their upper endpoints remain lower for tensor FVI at both horizons.
Tensor FVI has the tighter final all-state directed certificate at both horizons.
The complete-catalogue frontier is retrospective and does not implement a prospective stopping service.
Verification remains tensor-state dependent, exponential in horizon, and expensive even for d=2 and T<=3.
The adaptive cohort does not put the compiled witness on the least-work or lowest-cost frontier.
The approximate-null exercise uses known controlled perturbations rather than a learned or model-uncertain nullity procedure.
The finite frozen catalogue and single-host timings do not establish method-population reliability or general performance.
The executed normalized investment economy does not supply an Econometrica-scale substantive economic result.
The cumulative platform scope and document size remain disproportionate to the low-dimensional certification result.
limitations: The reviewer did not rerun policy construction, simulation, statistical inference, or timing services; new runs would create new observations.
The artifact audit verifies frozen records, PDF identities, release status, and aggregate arithmetic, not every inherited theorem line by line.
Single-host timing observations support no hardware-general performance inference.
No claim is made that tensor FVI dominates outside the declared R54 economies.
This advisory review is not an Econometric Society editorial decision.
positive_findings: R54 is a canonical source-bound publication with a successful clean rebuild.
The directed finite-sweep theorem appears internally coherent under its stated premises.
The theorem is executed at every decision date in the original continuous-law economy.
Actual policy cost rather than only a regret certificate is the primary endpoint.
Compiled-witness policies have strictly positive own-incumbent gains at T=2 and T=3.
Work, storage, actor ambiguity, pair recursion, and inference costs are exposed explicitly.
A stronger nonuniform conventional comparator and adverse method rankings are retained.
Controlled departures from exact action-null structure are tested and harmful false-null decisions are preserved.
recommendation: Reject in the present form and do not invite another ordinary revision of the cumulative manuscript. A new, sharply focused paper on directed safe policy improvement with coupled-residual verification in acquired-state dynamic programs could merit evaluation, but R54 does not establish a method-specific Econometrica-level numerical or economic advantage for Neural Bellman Operators.
